clue.text: A great address for a military adventurer

definitions.meaning: a very long speech made to hold up the passing of a law
an old sense: a freebooter who waged private war in foreign lands

explanation.surface: Someone praising a famous speech by a soldier of fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an obstructive marathon speech in a legislature and, historically, a privateer raiding Spanish America.

clue.text: Manuscript containing fine miscellany

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an olio is a mixed collection or hotchpotch

explanation.surface: A handwritten volume holding a fine assortment of pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a leaf or volume of a manuscript, so it stands for a manuscript book.

clue.text: Places where Mexican food's gobbled up by animals

indicators.note: something gobbled ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lions are big cats, animals

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a taco is a Mexican folded tortilla

explanation.surface: Somewhere zoo animals wolf down Mexican snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gobbled up by' reads as one phrase, but 'up' alone turns the snack (giving OCAT) and 'gobbled' sets it inside the animals; 'Places' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations are sites or spots, the plural noun matching places.

clue.text: Tropical country you said is in new Caribbean plan

indicators.note: one piece is said to sit within the other, a container signal
a new version of the letters is a rearrangement of them
said tells us to take how the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the word you is spoken like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tropical nation as part of a fresh plan for the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A banana republic is a small, often tropical state run on one export, a disparaging name for such a country.

clue.text: Understood economist's works

parts.note: saw in the sense 'I see' means understood
John Stuart Mill was a Victorian economist and philosopher

explanation.surface: A remark that one grasped an economist's writings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like an economist's books; it is a factory, a singular noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawmill is a plant where timber is cut, and works means a factory or plant.

clue.text: Artist has record quantity of beer

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
a stein is a large beer mug, and the measure it holds

explanation.surface: A painter who owns a record amount of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was a sculptor, an example of an artist.

clue.text: River enters another gorge

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, a container signal

parts.note: another river, the Cam at Cambridge
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A stream flows into a second ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to stuff oneself with food, a synonym of the verb gorge.

clue.text: Strange game

definitions.meaning: old British slang for odd or peculiar
a card game of collecting sets and runs

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both dated slang for odd and the name of a card game.

clue.text: Island fellow concocted diary

parts.note: the Isle of Man, a British island in the Irish Sea
F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

indicators.note: something concocted is made up, so these letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A castaway companion has made up a journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' rearranges F (fellow) with DIARY to make FRIDAY. In Defoe's Robinson Crusoe, Friday is the islander who becomes Crusoe's servant.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusoe's companion on his desert island was the native he named after a weekday, the whole clue describing him.

clue.text: Way in which many enter for exam

definitions.meaning: read literally, a shared doorway used by lots of people
the test taken for entry to British independent schools at 11 or 13

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is a shared doorway; it is also the admission test set by British fee-paying schools.

clue.text: Eastern capital invested once, making fortune today

parts.note: luck is fortune, good or bad
now means at the present time, today

explanation.surface: Money put into something long ago brings riches now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' means besieged, not financed: Lucknow, capital of Uttar Pradesh, was besieged in 1857.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city was under siege during the Mutiny, so it is a state capital in the East once surrounded by an army.

clue.text: Figures going up in winter after fall

definitions.text: Figures going up in winter after fall

parts.words: Figures going up in winter after fall
parts.note: figures sound like statistics rising after a drop; in fact they are shapes built outdoors after a snowfall

explanation.definitionFit: Children build these icy figures in the garden once snow has fallen.

clue.text: Clearly showing event is so special

indicators.note: a special arrangement of the letters signals that they are reordered

explanation.surface: Displaying plainly that an occasion is remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensive describes something that points out or demonstrates directly, displaying plainly.

clue.text: Henchard, for one, making runs with county

parts.note: Mayo is an Irish county
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A character scores runs alongside a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Henchard is the title figure of Hardy's novel The Mayor of Casterbridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Henchard holds civic office as head of the town council in Hardy's novel, an example of the role.

clue.text: This involves hearts of man and woman, for sure

definitions.text: This involves hearts of man and woman, for sure

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter or letters, taken from each word in turn

explanation.surface: A love affair surely engages the feelings of both partners.
explanation.walkthrough: Centres of man, woman, for and sure are A, M, O and UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair is something that engages the hearts of a man and a woman, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Presumably in favour of authentic choral music

definitions.meaning: read as two words, against what is fake, so supporting the genuine
music sung by two choirs answering each other

explanation.definitionFit: Split as anti-phony it means opposed to fakes; it is also responsive singing between two choirs.

clue.text: Leading Russian capital, with name changed

definitions.text: Leading Russian capital, with name changed

parts.words: Leading Russian capital, with name changed
parts.note: a former Russian capital renamed after a leading Russian revolutionary, and since renamed again

explanation.definitionFit: St Petersburg, once the capital, was renamed for the Soviet leader in 1924 and changed back in 1991.

clue.text: Sort of horse one trains with difficulty

indicators.note: letters arranged with difficulty are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: A trainer struggling with an awkward kind of horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosinante is Don Quixote's bony nag, so the name means a worn-out horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Don Quixote's steed is used for any broken-down nag, a kind of horse.

clue.text: International intrigue involving one high-flier, initially

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other, a container signal

parts.note: a plot is an intrigue or scheme
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cross-border conspiracy that drew in a successful person at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests an ambitious person, but it is someone who flies a new aircraft first.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot is the first to fly a new aircraft, a flier going up before anyone else.

clue.text: Permit too much freedom

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an authorisation document and excessive liberty of behaviour.

clue.text: Opposing points put in characteristic passage

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other, a container signal

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
N and S, north and south, are opposite compass points

explanation.surface: Contrary views are inserted into a typical section of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is the act of passing through, a passage from one place to another.

clue.text: Offensive refusal to include one of the best people

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it, a container signal

parts.note: nay is an old word for no, a refusal
ST abbreviates saint, one of the very best of people

explanation.surface: A rude rejection that takes in someone from the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty means unpleasant or objectionable, a synonym of offensive.

clue.text: Sound bishop joining the purple

parts.note: plum is a dark purple colour
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman is raised to the rank of cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining the purple' suggests promotion in the Church; it only sets B after PLUM.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to measure the depth of water with a weighted line, which is to sound it.

clue.text: Enemy vessel about to be destroyed

indicators.note: letters that are destroyed are broken up and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A hostile ship is on the point of being sunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat was a German submarine, an enemy craft to the Allies in both world wars.

clue.text: Bound, after king's intervention, to become annoyed

indicators.note: something that intervenes comes between, so it sits inside the other piece

parts.note: chained means tied up, bound
GR is George Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A captive is irritated when the monarch steps in.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrined describes someone vexed or mortified, a synonym of annoyed.

clue.text: People's protests cut short

definitions.meaning: the common people of a state, a Greek word

explanation.definitionFit: The word names the populace as a political body and is also the clipped plural of demonstrations.

clue.text: Dark blue, perhaps, is neat on Scotsman

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
taken as written
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A tidy drink served to a Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: Dark blue is the colour of Oxford University sport, so a Dark Blue is an Oxford man.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Oxford University teams are called Dark Blues, so an Oxford person is an example.

clue.text: Does for female rabbits, for example

definitions.text: Does for female rabbits, for example

parts.words: Does for female rabbits, for example
parts.note: reads as a verb about rabbits, but the word does is simply another term for female rabbits

explanation.definitionFit: Does means female rabbits, so one word standing in for another is an equivalent term.

clue.text: Highly elusive creature — however, one might be seen

parts.note: yet means however, nevertheless
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rarely spotted beast, though one might yet appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly' hints at the Himalayan heights where the creature is said to live.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a legendary beast seldom if ever sighted.

clue.text: Kind character takes fisherman's bait to loch

parts.note: a gentle is a maggot used as bait by anglers
Loch Ness is a famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: A good-natured angler carries his bait up to a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentleness is a mild and tender nature, a kindly disposition.
